transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-05 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Tom Baker (Redwood SE), Ava Patel (StellarBridge Head of ML), Markus Hoffmann (Eng Lead), Priya Singh (Product)

Summary: quick check of this week's eval gate results, a couple of surprising regressions on the persona prompts, discussion about guardrail strictness and an outline for a rollback tabletop + acceptance gates.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give folks another minute as people filter in, quick agenda - results from the last 72 hour run, a couple of low-confidence outputs, proposed guardrail tweaks, and then we want to confirm next steps and the rollback playbook.
00:28 Ava Patel: sounds good, sorry I'm late, train was a little delayed.
00:34 Diego Ramos: no worries. I pulled the spreadsheet into the call, here's the link in the chat - "benchmark_stellarbridge_v3.xlsx" - it's got per-prompt scoring and token latencies.
00:45 Markus Hoffmann: i saw an early note that a small subset of prompts are dropping in fidelity when we switch quantized model 8-bit variant, is that right?
00:55 Diego Ramos: yes, about 3% of the persona prompts fall under the threshold we set in sprint 1. To be precise, the score delta is roughly -0.12 on our BLEU-like metric and the confidence score is down. That said, throughput improved, median latency dropped from 210ms to 165ms for the common path.
01:20 Priya Singh: when you say persona prompts, which ones? the onboarding flow or the faq agent?
01:27 Diego Ramos: mostly onboarding and a handful from the policy assistant - the synthetic user 'mary' persona test set.
01:34 Ava Patel: hmm, those are high-priority, we can't degrade there. What's the root cause analysis so far?
01:40 Tom Baker: preliminary hypothesis is the KV cache warmup pattern plus continuous batching is interacting poorly with the 8-bit quantization for long-context prompts. We saw more attention truncation-like artifacts, some tokens missing — the transcript might mis-represent, but basically hallucination-style brevity.
02:05 Maya Chen: to unpack that: 8-bit quantization helps cost but changes numeric stability, combined with fallback batch sizes we suggested might be evicting important KV entries for persona continuity. Diego, can you say whether this is across all sequence lengths?
02:18 Diego Ramos: it's primarily >512 token sessions. Short sessions are fine. Also noticed that when we force smaller max-batch the issue reduces but cost goes up.
02:30 Markus Hoffmann: ok so it's a latency vs fidelity trade, classic. Could we restrict 8-bit to non-persona flows? can Redwood route based on prompt tags?
02:43 Maya Chen: yes — smart routing can send persona-tagged requests to a higher-precision variant or to a different instance pool. We can do route-based policies: tag -> model variant. There is a small cost delta though.
02:54 Ava Patel: what's the delta? we need ballpark for finance.
02:58 Maya Chen: roughly 20-25% higher token cost for the FP16 or 16-bit path versus 8-bit, but latency is stable and fidelity recovers. Diego will put concrete numbers in the sheet.
03:12 Diego Ramos: noted, I'll add a cost comparison column with sample distributions.
03:18 Priya Singh: another note — we surfaced a guardrail false positive where the safety filter blocked a benign user example in persona onboarding. Could that be due to new strictness thresholds?
03:27 Tom Baker: yes, the safety classifier model was bumped — we tuned to be conservative after a compliance ask. We can relax that threshold for a subset of endpoints but need to log the exceptions for audit.
03:38 Ava Patel: audit logs are mandatory for us, SOC-2 type needs. Redwood can provide audit logs?
03:44 Maya Chen: yes, Private and Dedicated both support audit trails, and hosted with the add-on retention we can export. We'll attach the security docs.
03:50 Markus Hoffmann: we have an infosec session next Friday; can we produce a short one-page summary of the change vectors and rollback steps?
03:58 Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll draft a rollback tabletop playbook and a one-pager.
04:05 Diego Ramos: wanted to call out one oddity in the eval — a cluster of examples where the model responded with outdated product names, looks like training data stale tokens or a prompt pattern mismatch. Example 123 in the spreadsheet shows the output "OldStack" instead of "StellarCore". Might be prompt prefix leakage in the caching layer.
04:28 Ava Patel: hmm that could be bad if it surfaces to customers. Any mitigation short-term?
04:32 Tom Baker: we can flush prefix cache for requests that match a certain regex and also apply prompt prevalidation — add a pre-prompt sanitizer to rewrite bad tokens. That's a config change, low risk.
04:45 Markus Hoffmann: are those changes backward compatible to production? we need to ensure no downtime for the pilot.
04:51 Diego Ramos: yes, they are non-breaking. We can rollout as a config with canary on 5% traffic then 25 then 100, and automatic rollback if error rate or regression metric crosses threshold.
05:06 Priya Singh: can you explain the acceptance gate metrics exactly? we have some internal KPIs.
05:12 Maya Chen: acceptance gates we propose: 1) no persona prompt average score drop >0.05 vs baseline, 2) safety false positive rate <= 0.8x current, 3) median token latency for primary flow <= 220ms, 4) fewer than 1% critical hallucination flags on the golden set. These are in the sheet too.
05:36 Ava Patel: that looks reasonable. The 0.05 delta is tight but okay. Do we have tooling to auto-evaluate and flag regressions?
05:43 Diego Ramos: yes, Redwood Optimize can run scheduled evals and produce heatmaps, but for this POC we're using a lightweight harness in the shared spreadsheet with sample IDs and diff flags. we'll hook Redwood Optimize if you want ongoing.
05:58 Markus Hoffmann: for the rollback playbook, who owns the decision to rollback? Eng or Product?
06:05 Priya Singh: product should sign off in consultation with eng. We'll require both signatures to execute a rollback in prod.
06:10 Maya Chen: noted — we'll add an approvals section: Eng lead + Product owner. We'll also include an emergency rollback path that Eng can trigger with post-hoc approvals for high-severity outages.
06:21 Ava Patel: can Redwood help run a tabletop so our oncall knows the procedures?
06:26 Lena Ortiz: yes, CS can facilitate a 60-min tabletop including incident triggers, runbook steps, and communication templates. We can aim for the week of Aug 11.
06:36 Markus Hoffmann: networking question — if we move to Dedicated pilot, what about egress and VPC peering? I've seen firewall rules block some health checks before.
06:46 Tom Baker: Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed NAT, we typically provide a small egress plan and a checklist. Diego can compile the network checklist items that previously tripped other customers.
06:56 Diego Ramos: will do, include sample CIDR, ports, TLS and mTLS options.
07:02 Priya Singh: security: what about KMS/HSM integration for keys at rest? required for certain customers.
07:08 Maya Chen: we support KMS integrations for Private; Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS in most regions — we'll confirm provider list in the security doc.
07:17 Ava Patel: okay good.
07:19 Diego Ramos: quick note on experiments: we ran a small A/B where the persona-tagging route sent traffic to a FP16 pool for 10% of sessions and KPI delta looks promising — persona scores recovered to baseline and latency was +/- 10ms. I'll add the A/B section to the sheet.
07:35 Markus Hoffmann: perfect, that suggests routing is the path forward rather than blanket reverting quantization.
07:40 Priya Singh: I want to make sure the golden set includes transactional privacy-sensitive prompts; can we mask PII during eval?
07:46 Tom Baker: yes, the harness supports PII redaction before storage and our logs can be configured to never persist raw prompt tokens. We'll document the config.
07:56 Maya Chen: to recap next steps - Redwood sends updated benchmark + cost delta and A/B results (action for Maya/Diego) by Aug 7, StellarBridge runs a 500-case regression on the persona golden set and returns low-confidence examples by Aug 8, schedule rollback tabletop for Aug 12 (CS to coordinate), and Markus to confirm infra items by Aug 11.
08:18 Ava Patel: sounds good. Also please include the exact canary policy we suggest, like 5/25/100 with 15m windows and a 2% regression trigger.
08:28 Diego Ramos: will add the canary policy details.
08:32 Maya Chen: any final questions?
08:35 Speaker 1 (unattributed): just a quick ask — can you include the sample HTTP payloads for persona tagging in the doc?
08:41 Diego Ramos: yep, sample payloads and tagging schema will be attached to the sheet.
08:46 Priya Singh: thanks everyone.
08:48 Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll send the artifacts and follow up on action items.
